title: Global integral lattices for lisse sheaves on smooth geometric fibres
statement: Let $K_0\subseteq K$ be fields, let $T_0$ be a smooth separated finite-type $K_0$-scheme [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], and put $T=T_0\times_{K_0}K$ [def-pc-base-change]. Let $\ell$ be a prime invertible in $K_0$, let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be finite with valuation ring $A=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and on $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] put $B_T=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}(A/\varpi^n)_T$ and $E_T=B_T[1/\varpi]$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. For every $E_T$-module sheaf $L$ which is pro-etale locally finite free [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], there is a $B_T$-submodule sheaf $M\subseteq L$, pro-etale locally finite free, such that the inclusion induces an isomorphism $M[1/\varpi]\xrightarrow{\sim}L$. The ranks may vary between components and may be zero; the empty scheme is included.

source.place: Lemmas 7.4.7 and 7.4.10, pp. 70-71, and Proposition 6.8.4(1),(4), pp. 59-60; geometric input: Stacks varieties.tex Tag 056T (lemma-smooth-geometrically-normal), morphisms.tex Tag 01VB (lemma-base-change-smooth), properties.tex Tag 0BQ3 (lemma-normal-geometrically-unibranch). Compact profinite monodromy admits an integral lattice.

proof.text: By [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change], $T$ is separated and finite type over $K$. The spectrum of a field is Noetherian: its one affine chart has only the ideals $0$ and $(1)$. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $T$ Noetherian. Apply [lem-trf-smooth-geometrically-normal] to the smooth $K_0$-scheme $T_0$ and the given field extension $K/K_0$: every local ring of $T$ is a normal domain. Finally $\ell$ remains invertible in $K$ and in all local rings of $T$, since its inverse in $K_0$ maps to an inverse. No finite-type hypothesis on $K/K_0$ is needed.

source.place: Tag 056T, lemma-smooth-geometrically-normal; morphisms.tex Tags 01T4 and 01T6; schemes.tex Tag 01KU

proof.text: Apply [lem-a1-normal-completed-integral-model] to $T$, its normal stalks, the unit $\ell$, and the recorded constant uniformizer section. Obtain a locally finite free integral model $M$ and a scalar-extension isomorphism $e:M[1/\varpi]\cong L$. This supplies only an abstract model, so an embedding remains to be proved.

source.place: Lemmas 7.4.7 and 7.4.10, pp. 70-71, and Proposition 6.8.4(1),(4), pp. 59-60; geometric input: Stacks varieties.tex Tag 056T (lemma-smooth-geometrically-normal), morphisms.tex Tag 01VB (lemma-base-change-smooth), properties.tex Tag 0BQ3 (lemma-normal-geometrically-unibranch). Compact profinite monodromy admits an integral lattice.

proof.text: Multiplication by $\varpi$ is injective on $B_T$. In a domain, if $\varpi x=0$ modulo $\varpi^{n+2}$, cancelling the nonzero $\varpi$ shows that $x$ maps to zero modulo $\varpi^{n+1}$. This statement passes to constant sheafifications: lift a section locally to a constant, then refine once more so its annihilator equation holds in the original ring, and use separatedness to descend its zero image. Applying this to all adjacent levels of the completed limit makes every projection of a $\varpi$-annihilated section zero. The recorded DVR generator is nonzero because it generates the nonzero maximal ideal. Thus all powers of the uniformizer are regular. Sectionwise localization is injective, and sheafification preserves this injectivity: equality after sheafification holds in the localizations on a covering, hence in $B_T$ there, and then globally by separatedness.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2(1),(2), proved directly for the recorded constant quotient limit

proof.text: Define $i:M\to\operatorname{Res}(L)$ as the adjoint of $e$: on sections it sends $m$ to $e(1\otimes m)$, with the tensor presheaf followed by its sheafification unit. Naturality and the defining pure-tensor equation follow from this adjunction. To prove injectivity, equality of images gives equality after sheafification of $1\otimes m$ and $1\otimes n$, hence equality on a covering in the tensor presheaf. Refine by a finite free chart for $M$. On this chart tensoring its basis identifies this map with a finite product of the injective coefficient localization maps, so the two restricted sections coincide. The sheaf separatedness condition gives $m=n$. Sectionwise injectivity gives that $i$ is monic. The original local freeness of $M$, the given isomorphism $e$, and its defining tensor equation give precisely the required witnesses. No image object or arbitrary integral witness is used in a definition.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2(2) and Definition 6.8.3; torsion-free localization on finite free charts

tool_uses.why: Generic base-change permanence supplies separated finite type over K; this unit has no such scheme-theoretic tool.
Generic Noetherian permanence for finite-type schemes supplies the Noetherian base of monodromy.
Generic smooth-over-a-field normality, applied to T_0 and K/K_0, is a geometry tool, not a trace-formula argument.
Generic topology gives finitely many clopen connected components; there is no replacement in this unit.
Generic compact continuous representation lattice theorem is the algebra tool after profinite monodromy.
Only finite-coefficient clause (1) is used, to realize the quotient representations as a normalized tower.
Integral completion of a normalized finite locally free etale tower supplies the completed lisse sheaf; no affine-curve cohomology or perverse theorem is used.
Only its canonical coefficient ring isomorphisms identify the completed ring with the continuous-function ring.
